resources.string: SpeakerLink needs the \"Nearby devices\" permission to find, pair and connect your speakers. It never uses it to work out your location, and the app has no internet access.
On this Android version, finding Bluetooth devices requires the location permission. SpeakerLink never uses your location, and the app has no internet access.
Turn on Bluetooth to see and connect your speakers.
Up to %1$d Bluetooth audio devices can be connected at once.
No speaker is playing right now
Android sends music to one Bluetooth speaker at a time. To play on several JBL speakers together, link them on the Party tab.
No paired JBL speakers yet. Tap Scan and put a speaker in pairing mode.
Searching for speakers in pairing mode…
Hold the speaker\'s Bluetooth button until its light blinks (pairing mode), then tap Scan.
Also nearby, but not in pairing mode: %1$s
No speakers in pairing mode found.
Couldn\'t reach the speaker\'s control service.
This speaker doesn\'t offer the JBL control service.
The speaker didn\'t answer. Close the JBL app on other phones and try again.
The Nearby devices permission is missing.
The speaker answered but did not report its battery.
Battery and info use JBL\'s unofficial control protocol and may not work on every model.
Pick the model if SpeakerLink got it wrong, for example after the speaker was renamed.
Up to %1$d speakers in one group

Your phone streams to one speaker, the host. The other JBL speakers get the music from the host over their own link (PartyBoost, Auracast or Connect+). Speakers of different link systems can\'t be in the same group.
Pair your JBL speakers on the Speakers tab first.
Switch every speaker on and put them close together.
Connect your phone to %1$s. Only the host needs a Bluetooth connection to the phone.
Within about 30 seconds, press the %1$s button on %2$s.
Start TWS pairing on %1$s as described in its manual.
Both speakers are the same model, so you can choose Stereo (left and right) instead of Party mode in JBL\'s app.
All speakers play the same music (Party mode). Stereo needs exactly two speakers of the same model.
Play music on your phone. Every speaker in the group plays it.
The Charge 3 links with Connect+ speakers only after its firmware update.
A speaker here supports two link systems (Xtreme 4, PartyBox Club 120 or Stage 320). It was put in this group and can be in only one group at a time.
Newer PartyBoxes get Auracast and linking with other speakers through firmware updates in JBL\'s PartyBox app.
Linking support of at least one model here is not confirmed.
These speakers use different link systems, so they can\'t all play in one group.
Unknown model. Set the model in the speaker\'s menu on the Speakers tab.
It\'s unclear whether this model can link with other speakers.
This model can\'t link with other speakers.
The %1$s group is full (at most %2$d speakers).
Tip: play the test sound. Every linked speaker should chime.
Other ways to use several speakers
Galaxy phones can stream to two Bluetooth speakers at once, even of different generations. Connect both, open the media output panel and select both speakers.
Android can share audio with up to two LE Audio devices. Most JBL portables can\'t receive it, so it is mainly for LE Audio headphones and speakers.
Keep several speakers connected and move the music between them with one tap on the Speakers tab.
SpeakerLink pairs and connects several JBL Bluetooth speakers, shows which one is playing, and walks you through linking them with PartyBoost, Auracast or Connect+.

SpeakerLink is an independent open-source app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by JBL or HARMAN International. JBL, PartyBoost and Connect+ are trademarks of HARMAN International Industries, Incorporated. Auracast is a trademark of the Bluetooth SIG.
SpeakerLink has no internet permission, no ads and no tracking. Everything stays on your phone.
